decisions.reason: GA4 is Google's current analytics standard, so the plugin fits the firm's analytics and conversion offering, and demand from shop clients should only grow.
Google shut down Universal Analytics, so the plugin's decline cannot be blamed on temporary causes, and it was only mentioned in passing, so little would have to be written off or justified.
Interface plugins are central to the firm's integration expertise and cost little to maintain, so there is no reason to give up an investment that still serves shop clients.
The service has its own page, a visible public commitment, and it ties directly to the firm's core relaunch and SEO business, so dropping it would expose the earlier decision without a clear reason.
